correctness.rationale: Conditioning on a prescribed r-cycle gives exactly r vertices with 1+Bin(n-r,1/n) indegree and n-r vertices with Bin(n-r,1/n) indegree. The resulting mixed moment minus the unconditional binomial mean produces P_n(r). The difference P_n(r+1)-aP_n(r)=r[n^2-n-(2n-1)r-r^2]/n makes the scaled sign function unimodal. Its initial equality and strict rise for n>=4, final zero, and coprime divisibility excluding any r>=3 equality prove the unique sign switch. Limiting normalized scaled sign F_n(floor(nx))/n^3=(1-x)(1+x^2)e^x has unique interior crossing by explicit derivative. An independent program enumerated all 50,068 maps with n<=6 and completed 11,828 exact rational tests, with no discrepancies. Small n=2,3 handled separately; finite enumeration does not prove the infinite theorem.

value.rationale: The indegree-two count is a canonical statistic of binary merging/branching in functional graph components, while the number of length-r recurrent cycles probes global core scale. The theorem gives the full finite dependence spectrum, an unexpectedly sharp positive-to-negative threshold, and a nontrivial universal 0.584724... asymptotic cutoff. Marginal counts do not determine the covariance. The scope is a natural full parameter family, not an arbitrary slice or a tiny improvement.
